thought_title: If he only seemed to suffer, why am I in chains?

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Εἰ δέ, ὥσπερ τινὲς ἄθεοι ὄντες, τουτέστιν ἄπιστοι, λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν πεπονθέναι αὐτόν, αὐτοὶ ὄντες τὸ δοκεῖν, ἐγὼ τί δέδεμαι, τί δὲ καὶ εὔχομαι θηριομαχῆσαι; δωρεὰν οὖν ἀποθνήσκω. ἄρα οὖν καταψεύδομαι τοῦ κυρίου.
pass_a_gloss: If, however, as certain people who are without God (that is, unbelievers) say, his suffering was only in appearance, they themselves being mere appearance, why have I been bound, and why do I even pray to fight with wild beasts? In that case I am dying for nothing. So then I am speaking falsely against the Lord.

lemmas.gloss: bind; perfect passive: be in chains

pass_b_english: But if, as some say who are godless, that is, faithless, he only seemed to suffer (they are the ones who only seem!), why am I in chains? Why do I even pray to fight the beasts? Then I die for nothing. Then I am lying about the Lord.

choices.term: τὸ δοκεῖν πεπονθέναι … αὐτοὶ ὄντες τὸ δοκεῖν
choices.english: he only seemed to suffer (they are the ones who only seem!)
choices.why: Ignatius turns the docetists' key word back on them; the exclamation keeps his scorn in plain speech.
rejected: suffered only in appearance … they themselves being appearance (stiff)

choices.why: ἄθεος here is moral-religious, not modern atheism; 'faithless' carries ἄπιστος and keeps the paired sound.
Literal arena combat Ignatius expects in Rome.
rejected: fight with beasts at Ephesus (Pauline phrase not present)

choices.english: I am lying about the Lord
choices.why: κατα- + genitive: false witness against the Lord; 'lying about' is the natural English.

anf_compare.notes: ANF and Lake agree; owner game draft kept verbatim.

notes: Possible echoes, not tagged inline: Galatians 2:21 (Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν, 'died for nothing'); 1 Corinthians 15:14–15 (preaching in vain, false witnesses about God). Wording overlap is partial.
Owner's game draft used unchanged; it is accurate to Lake.

review.notes: Checked paragraph 1 against both passes. Locked Greek: «Εἰ δέ, ὥσπερ τινὲς ἄθεοι ὄντες, τουτέστιν ἄπιστοι, λέγουσιν, τὸ δοκεῖν πεπονθέναι αὐτόν, αὐτοὶ ὄντες τὸ δοκεῖν, ἐγὼ τί δέδεμαι, τί δὲ καὶ εὔχομαι θηριομαχῆσαι; δωρεὰν οὖν ἀποθνήσκω. ἄρα οὖν καταψεύδομαι τοῦ κυρίου.» This is Trallians 10, not a paraphrase. Pass A keeps the conditional, the τουτέστιν pair, the retort that they themselves are τὸ δοκεῖν, both questions, and both inferential conclusions («why have I been bound, and why do I even pray to fight with wild beasts? In that case I am dying for nothing. So then I am speaking falsely against the Lord»). Pass B neither adds nor reverses those clauses: «he only seemed to suffer (they are the ones who only seem!)» and «Then I am lying about the Lord» stay inside the reductio. No inline citation is present to mismatch; partial echoes are disclosed as untagged. Title names the thought.
